subject: Svenska
title: Writing rules and correct Swedish
sourceSummary: De and dem, särskrivning (incorrect word splitting), comma placement and capital letters — the most common mistakes that lower your grade on written assignments.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "___ sprang hela vägen till skolan."
questions.opener: Substitute the word with English "they" or "them" — which one fits?
questions.explanation: The word is the subject (it's them who are running) — the subject form is "de". Test: "they ran", not "them ran".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Jag pratade med ___ på rasten."
questions.opener: The word comes after a preposition ("med") — which form does that require?
questions.explanation: After prepositions (med, till, för, av...) the object form is always used: "dem". Test: "with them", not "with they".

questions.opener: A compound word is ONE thing — not two separate words side by side.
choices: Vi åt en jord gubbs tårta.
questions.explanation: "Jordgubbstårta" is a compound word and should be written as one word. Splitting it up (särskrivning) can change the meaning: "jordgubbs tårta" sounds like a cake that BELONGS TO the strawberries.

questions.prompt: What does "en rödhårig flicka" mean compared to "en röd hårig flicka"?
questions.opener: Read the two phrases aloud and listen for the difference.
choices: Rödhårig = has red hair. Röd hårig = the girl is red and hairy.
Röd hårig is correct, rödhårig is wrong
There is no difference in writing, only in speech
questions.explanation: Splitting the word up (särskrivning) changes the meaning: "rödhårig" is a compound adjective (red hair), while "röd, hårig" describes the girl as both red AND hairy — a completely different picture.

questions.prompt: Where should the comma be placed? "Innan vi gick hemifrån ___ kollade vi att spisen var avstängd."
questions.opener: A subordinate clause that comes BEFORE the main clause is often closed off with a comma.
questions.explanation: "Innan vi gick hemifrån" is a subordinate clause that comes first in the sentence — it's closed off with a comma before the main clause begins: "...hemifrån, kollade vi..."

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
questions.opener: Capital letters are used for proper nouns — not for common nouns, seasons or compass directions.
choices: Jag älskar Sommaren mest av alla Årstider.
Vi åkte till Stockholm i somras.
Vi bor i Norra delen av Sverige.
questions.explanation: "Stockholm" is a proper noun (a place) and should be capitalised. Seasons, family words (mamma) and occupations (lärare) are written with a lowercase letter unless they begin a sentence.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence and explain each change: "Läraren gav de som var färdiga extra uppgifter, dom andra fick jord gubbs saft medans dem väntade."
questions.opener: Look for four mistakes: a de/dem error, "dom" in writing, incorrect word splitting (särskrivning), and a run-on sentence.
questions.answer: Läraren gav dem som var färdiga extra uppgifter. De andra fick jordgubbssaft medan de väntade.
steps: "gav de som var färdiga" → "gav dem som var färdiga". After the verb "gav" (to whom?) the object form is required.
"dom andra" → "de andra". "Dom" is a spoken-language form and is avoided in writing; here the word is also the subject.
"jord gubbs saft" → "jordgubbssaft". A compound word is written as one word, not as three separate words.
"medans dem väntade" → "medan de väntade". "Medans" is an incorrect form of "medan", and the word is the subject in the subordinate clause (de väntade) — not dem.
The sentence was also split with a full stop after "uppgifter" to avoid an overly long, hard-to-read sentence (a run-on sentence).

questions.prompt: What tricks can you use to write correctly: de/dem, särskrivning and capital letters?
questions.answer: De/dem: substitute with they/them (or we/us) — if it becomes "they"/"we" you write "de", if it becomes "them"/"us" you write "dem". After a preposition (med, till, för, av) it's always "dem". Särskrivning: ask whether the words form ONE connected meaning — if so, they're written as one word (jordgubbstårta, glasögonfodral). Capital letters: only for proper nouns (people, places, companies, the first word of a sentence) — not for occupations, family words or seasons.
